question: All cats are animals. All animals are living things. Which conclusion is definitely true?

options.D: No cat is a living thing

explanation: Universal affirmative syllogism: All A→B, All B→C, therefore All A→C. All cats are animals, all animals are living things, so all cats are living things.

question: No birds are fish. Some fish are cold-blooded. Which conclusion follows?

options.C: Some cold-blooded things are not birds

explanation: Since some fish are cold-blooded and no birds are fish, those fish (cold-blooded) are definitely not birds. So some cold-blooded things are not birds.

question: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red. Which statement must be true?
explanation: Since 'some flowers are red' doesn't specify which flowers, and there may be flowers that are not roses, 'some flowers are not roses' can be concluded as roses are only a subset.

question: All doctors are graduates. Some graduates are rich. No rich person is poor. Which conclusion is valid?
explanation: Some graduates are rich, and no rich person is poor, so those rich graduates are not poor. Therefore, some graduates are not poor.

question: Some pens are books. All books are stationery. Some stationery are expensive. Which conclusion definitely follows?
explanation: Some pens are books (given). All books are stationery. So those pens that are books are also stationery. Therefore, some pens are stationery.

question: No manager is an engineer. All engineers are technical staff. Some technical staff are experienced. Which conclusion is INVALID?

options.A: Some technical staff are not managers
options.C: Some experienced people are technical staff

explanation: We know no manager is an engineer, but technical staff includes engineers AND possibly others. A manager could be technical staff without being an engineer. So 'No manager is technical staff' is not necessarily valid.

question: All A are B. No B is C. Some C are D. All D are E. Which of the following must be true?
explanation: No B is C; Some C are D; All D are E. So some D are not B, and since all D are E, some E are not B. Also, No A is C follows from All A are B and No B is C.

question: If it rains, then the match is cancelled. The match is cancelled. What can we conclude?

options.C: It may or may not have rained

explanation: This is the fallacy of affirming the consequent. If P→Q and Q is true, P may or may not be true. The match could be cancelled for other reasons.

question: If a student studies hard, they pass the exam. Raza did not pass the exam. What follows?

options.D: Some students who study hard fail

explanation: Modus tollens: If P→Q, and not-Q, then not-P. If studying hard → passing, and Raza didn't pass, then Raza didn't study hard.

question: If Ali goes to the market, he buys fruit. If he buys fruit, he makes juice. Ali did not make juice. Which conclusion is valid?

options.A: Ali went to the market but didn't buy fruit
options.B: Ali did not go to the market
options.D: Ali bought fruit but didn't make juice

explanation: Chain: Market→Fruit→Juice. Contrapositive: Not juice→Not fruit→Not market. Since no juice, Ali did not go to the market.

question: Only if a project has a deadline, it gets prioritized. Project X gets prioritized. Which must be true?

options.B: All projects with deadlines are prioritized
options.D: Some projects without deadlines are prioritized

explanation: 'Only if P, then Q' means Q→P. If prioritized→has deadline. Project X is prioritized, so Project X has a deadline.

question: If the temperature exceeds 40°C, the factory shuts down. If the factory shuts down, workers go home. Today workers did not go home. Which is true?

options.B: Factory shut down but workers stayed

explanation: Workers not going home → factory didn't shut down → temperature didn't exceed 40°C (contrapositive chain).

question: Statements: (1) If X, then Y. (2) If Y, then not Z. (3) If not Z, then W. (4) W is false. Which must be false?
explanation: W is false → not-W → not (not Z) → Z is true → not Y (from statement 2 contrapositive) → not X (from statement 1 contrapositive). So both X and Y are false.

question: Argument: Students who sleep 8 hours perform better academically than those who sleep less. Which strengthens this?

options.A: Some students sleep 10 hours and perform poorly
options.B: A study of 5,000 students confirms 8-hour sleepers have 20% higher GPAs
options.C: Sleep quality matters more than quantity
options.D: Academic performance depends only on study time

explanation: A large-scale study directly confirming the argument's claim with statistical evidence strengthens it most directly.

question: Argument: Reducing screen time improves children's attention spans. Which weakens this?

options.A: Many children who use screens do well in school
options.B: Studies show no significant attention span difference between low and high screen users when controlling for other factors
options.C: Some parents limit screen time effectively
options.D: Attention spans vary naturally among children

explanation: Controlled studies showing no difference directly undermine the causal claim between screen time and attention spans.

question: Argument: The new traffic law reduced accidents by 30% in City A, so it should be implemented in City B. Which most weakens this?

options.A: City B has more cars than City A
options.B: City B already has a lower accident rate than City A had before the law
options.C: The law was controversial in City A
options.D: City A took 2 years to see results

explanation: If City B already has a lower accident rate, the law's benefits may not apply—there's less room for improvement, undermining the case for implementation.

question: Argument: Company X's profits rose after switching to remote work, proving remote work increases productivity. Which assumption does this argument make?

options.B: No other factors caused the profit increase
options.D: Office rent savings caused the profit rise

explanation: The argument assumes the profit rise was solely due to productivity gains from remote work, ignoring confounding variables like cost savings or market conditions.

question: Conclusion: Regular exercise prevents depression. Evidence: Depressed people exercise less than non-depressed people. The main flaw is:

options.A: The sample size is too small
options.B: Correlation is confused with causation; depression may cause less exercise

explanation: The evidence shows correlation but the argument claims causation. Depression itself may be causing reduced exercise rather than lack of exercise causing depression—reverse causality.

question: Argument: Since violent crime in Karachi fell 15% after more police were deployed, increasing police presence reduces crime. Which best strengthens this while addressing alternative explanations?

options.A: Other cities with more police also saw crime reductions
options.B: Crime fell only in areas with new police deployment, not elsewhere in Karachi during the same period
options.C: Residents reported feeling safer after deployment

explanation: Showing crime fell specifically in deployment areas but not elsewhere controls for other city-wide factors (economy, season), isolating police presence as the causal factor.

question: Statement: We should ban junk food advertisements targeting children to reduce childhood obesity. The underlying assumption is:

options.B: Junk food advertisements influence children's eating choices

explanation: The recommendation only makes sense if advertisements actually affect what children eat. This is the necessary, unstated assumption.

question: Argument: Farhan scored 95% on his math test, so he will definitely get an A in the course. What is assumed?

options.A: The math test is the only assessment in the course
options.B: A 95% score qualifies for an A grade

explanation: The conclusion that he gets an A assumes a 95% qualifies for that grade. Without this assumption, the conclusion doesn't follow.

question: Argument: This medicine cured patients in clinical trials, so it will help you recover. Which assumption is necessary for this conclusion?

options.A: The medicine has no side effects
options.B: Your condition is similar to that of the trial patients

explanation: For the medicine to help this specific person, their condition must be sufficiently similar to those in the trial. Without this, extrapolating trial results is unjustified.

question: Proposal: Build a new highway to reduce travel time between City P and City Q. The proposal assumes:

options.A: The highway will be completed on time
options.B: Current travel time is unacceptably long
options.C: Traffic congestion is the main cause of current delays
options.D: Residents of both cities want faster travel

explanation: A highway reduces congestion-related delays. If delays are caused by other factors (road quality, traffic signals), the highway may not help. The proposal assumes congestion is the root cause.

question: Argument: Since our product's 5-star reviews doubled last quarter, customer satisfaction has improved. The critical assumption is:

options.A: Five-star reviews accurately reflect customer satisfaction
options.B: The company sells more products each quarter
options.C: Customers who are dissatisfied don't leave reviews

explanation: The argument assumes reviews are a reliable measure of actual satisfaction. If many reviews are fake or incentivized, the conclusion fails.

question: Argument: Nations with higher chocolate consumption have more Nobel Prize winners per capita. Therefore, eating chocolate boosts cognitive performance. Which assumption is most critical to evaluate?

options.B: Wealthy nations can afford both chocolate and research funding
options.D: The correlation exists across all age groups

explanation: If wealth drives both chocolate consumption and Nobel research funding, it's a confounding variable. The critical assumption is that wealth (a third variable) is NOT the actual cause—which may be false.

question: Paradox: A hospital introduced hand-washing protocols. Hospital-acquired infection rates initially INCREASED for two months before declining. Which best explains this?

options.C: Better monitoring after the protocol was introduced detected previously unreported infections

explanation: Better awareness and monitoring after protocol introduction led to infections being reported that were previously going unrecorded, giving a false initial appearance of increase.

question: Paradox: A city installed speed bumps on a dangerous road. Accidents on that road decreased, but accidents in the surrounding neighborhood increased. Which best explains this?

options.B: Drivers avoided the road with speed bumps and used smaller neighborhood streets, increasing risk there
options.C: Neighborhood roads are naturally more dangerous
options.D: Accident reporting improved in the neighborhood

explanation: Speed bumps diverted traffic to alternative neighborhood roads not designed for high traffic volume, shifting rather than reducing accident risk.

question: Paradox: Country X increased its education budget by 40% over 10 years, but literacy rates only improved by 2%. Which resolution is most plausible?

options.A: Education is not important for literacy
options.B: The budget increase went primarily to university research and infrastructure, not primary literacy programs
options.C: Teachers became less effective after the increase

explanation: If funds were misallocated to non-literacy areas (universities, buildings), the core literacy issue remains unaddressed, explaining minimal improvement despite large spending.

question: Paradox: Sales of luxury cars rose significantly during an economic recession. Which explanation best resolves this?

options.A: People made poor financial decisions during the recession
options.B: While the middle class suffered, wealthy individuals were largely unaffected and continued discretionary spending
options.C: Luxury cars became cheaper during the recession
options.D: Public transport failed during the recession

explanation: Recessions don't affect all income groups equally. The top wealth tier, insulated from job losses, continued or even increased luxury spending while middle-class spending fell.

question: A store sold 120 units in January, 150 in February, and 90 in March. What was the average monthly sales for this quarter?
A pie chart shows: Science 30%, Arts 25%, Commerce 35%, Others 10%. In a school of 800 students, how many are in Commerce?
explanation: Commerce students = 35% of 800 = 0.35 × 800 = 280.

question: Sales data: 2020: 200, 2021: 250, 2022: 300, 2023: 280. What is the percentage change from 2021 to 2023?
A bar graph shows expenses: Rent 40%, Food 25%, Transport 15%, Misc 20%. If total monthly expenses are Rs. 50,000, how much more is spent on Rent than Transport?
Table shows pass rates: School A: 75%, School B: 82%, School C: 68%, School D: 90%. If all schools have 200 students each, how many students failed across all schools?
Revenue (Rs. millions): Q1=12, Q2=15, Q3=18, Q4=9. Costs are 60% of revenue each quarter. What is the annual profit margin (profit/revenue × 100)?
explanation: Total revenue = 54M. Total cost = 60% × 54 = 32.4M. Profit = 54-32.4 = 21.6M. Margin = 21.6/54 × 100 = 40%.

question: Five people A, B, C, D, E sit in a row. A is at one end, E is next to A, B is at the other end. Who can be in the middle?
explanation: Arrangement: A-E-?-?-B. The middle position (3rd) and 4th position are occupied by C and D in some order, so C or D can be in the middle.

question: Six books P, Q, R, S, T, U are on a shelf. P is 3rd, T is immediately right of P, Q is at one end, R is between Q and P. Where is S?
explanation: Q is at one end (1st), R is between Q and P: Q(1)-R(2)-P(3)-T(4). U and S fill positions 5 and 6 in any order, so S is 5th or 6th.

question: Seven students are ranked 1–7. Ayesha is ranked 3rd. Bilal is ranked 2 places above Ayesha. Zara is ranked exactly between Bilal and Ayesha. What is Zara's rank?
explanation: Ayesha = 3rd. Bilal is 2 above = 1st. Between ranks 1 and 3 is rank 2. So Zara is 2nd.

question: Eight houses are in a row numbered 1-8. Conditions: Red house is immediately left of blue. Green is 3 houses from red. Yellow is at an end. Blue is not at position 8. Red is not positions 1, 2, or 7. How many valid positions exist for red?
explanation: Red cannot be 1,2,7. Blue=Red+1, so Red cannot be 8. Red≠7 and blue≠8 means Red≠7. Valid positions: 3,4,5,6. Green is 3 away from red: Red=3→Green=6; Red=4→Green=1 or 7; Red=5→Green=2 or 8; Red=6→Green=3 or 9(invalid). All work with yellow at an end. So 2 positions (3 and 6) satisfy all constraints cleanly.

question: 4 people A, B, C, D sit around a circular table. A sits opposite C. B and D are adjacent to A. Who sits opposite B?
explanation: Arrangement: A opposite C, B and D on either side of A. So B opposite D (they are across the table from each other).

question: 6 friends P, Q, R, S, T, U sit in a circle. P is between Q and R. T is opposite P. S is immediately right of T. Who is immediately left of Q?
explanation: Fixing P between Q and R: Q-P-R (or R-P-Q). T opposite P. S right of T. Remaining U fills the last spot. Working through the circle, U is immediately left of Q.

question: 5 people sit in a circle. In how many distinct arrangements can they sit (considering rotations as the same)?
explanation: Circular arrangements = (n-1)! = (5-1)! = 4! = 24.

question: 8 people sit in a circle. A must not sit next to B. B must sit next to C. How many valid arrangements exist (as a fraction of total circular arrangements)?
explanation: Total circular arrangements = 7!. Arrangements with B next to C: treat BC as unit → 6! × 2. Of these, subtract those where A is next to B: arrangements with A next to B (with BC together) = 5! × 2 × 2 (for BC and AB-BC configurations). Valid = 7! - [A next to B arrangements]. Ratio simplifies to 5/7 of total valid BC-together arrangements.

question: A is B's father. C is A's sister. What is C's relationship to B?
explanation: A is B's father. C is A's sister. So C is the sister of B's father, which makes C B's aunt.

question: Pointing to a photo, Sara says 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the person in the photo related to Sara?
explanation: The only daughter of Sara's mother is Sara herself. So his mother is Sara. Therefore, the person in the photo is Sara's son.

question: X is Y's brother. Y is Z's sister. Z is W's son. W is V's husband. How is X related to V?
explanation: Z is W's son. Y is Z's sister, so Y is also W's child. X is Y's brother, so X is also W's child. V is W's wife (husband means W and V are spouses). So X is V's son.

question: In a family, there are 2 couples. One couple's son is the other couple's daughter's husband. How many people are in the family?
explanation: Couple 1: parents of a son. Couple 2: parents of a daughter. The son married the daughter, forming couple 3. Total: Couple 1 (2) + Couple 2 (2) + the son (already counted in couple 1's son) + daughter. Total distinct people = 6 (father1, mother1, son + father2, mother2, daughter = the son and daughter being the married couple).

question: A says 'B is my son's wife's husband's brother.' What is B's relation to A?
explanation: A's son's wife's husband = A's son (a wife's husband is the son himself). A's son's brother = A's other son. So B is A's son.

question: Sara walks 5 km North, then turns right and walks 3 km. Which direction is she facing now?
explanation: Starting facing North, turning right changes direction to East.

question: A man faces South. He turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anti-clockwise. Which direction does he now face?
explanation: Facing South, turn 90° clockwise → face West. Turn 180° anti-clockwise from West → face East.
